title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Extra Pattern Detection on Teron 640
subtitle: Post-Oxidation Quality Validation for 65nm Node Manufacturing
author: James Rodriguez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron 640 system to detect and classify Extra Pattern defects during post-oxidation inspection at the 65nm technology node. The test is conducted at Dresden Fab 3 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Extra Pattern defects that are critical to yield at the 65nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron 640 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron 640
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Extra Pattern
- Process Step: Post-Oxidation
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 65nm
- Fab Location: Dresden Fab 3

This test case applies to all Teron 640 systems deployed at Dresden Fab 3 for post-oxidation monitoring in the 65nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron 640
Software Version: v10.0.373
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_65nm_POST_OXIDATION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (123 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron 640 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Extra Pattern defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 65nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 72 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 96% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.0% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-06-22
Wafers Tested: 29
Total Defects Found: 693
Defect Density: 220.59 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.3%
Capture Rate: 91.7%
Test Duration: 359 minutes
System Uptime: 97.8%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron 640 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Extra Pattern at the 65nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
